It is settled proposition of law that, in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine-qua-non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.
A holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an enquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

However, that does not mean that a Tribunal which has been approached with a claim for compensation under the Motor Vehicles Act should ignore all basic principles of law in determining the claim for compensation.
The relevant provisions of the Act are not intended to jettison all principles of law relating to a claim for compensation, which is still based on a tortious liability.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi B h u t a n i ______________________________________________________________________ MACT no. 119/22 (Attached DAR-MACT no.216/22) Shyam Sunder v. Neeraj & Ors. 5 of 21 Pages &

14. In the cross-examination of PW1 (petitioner) conduced on 09.08.2023, he admitted that the date of the accident was 19.03.2022 and that he did not tell the registration number of the offending vehicle or its particulars to the Investigating Officer on the date of the accident.

PW2 further stated that he had disclosed the identity of the offending vehicle and its registration number only after 2 days of the accident, i.e., on 21.03.2022 to the Investigating Officer of the case.

15. Delay in registration of FIR is not always fatal; however, the delay in registration of FIR has to be explained and if the reason is not cogent for the delay, it leads to the presumption that there is the possibility of embellishment, concoction and false implication.
The Investigating Officer of the criminal case which was registered regarding the accident has been examined as the court witness CW1.

CW1 has deposed that, on 19.03.2022 at about 03:30 p.m.,
there was a PCR call which was marked to him. Thereafter, he went to the spot of the accident, i.e.,
Mandoli Road, Delhi, where he did not meet anyone.

In the complaint on the basis of which the subject FIR has been lodged, the registration number of the offending vehicle has been mentioned by the petitioner and as there was delay in the registration of FIR, the logical question arises how the registration number of the offending vehicle in the FIR came to be mentioned.
23. As per the complaint/ FIR, when the petitioner was made to sit on the footpath after the accident, he noted down the registration number of the offending vehicle.

The words noted down could have two connotations: first noted in the memory and second, noted down on some object/
piece of paper, etc.

To the Court question put to the Investigating Officer whether the petitioner/injured told the registration number of the offending vehicle orally or from his memory to the Investigating Officer, the Investigating Officer replied that the injured did not refer any written note or any device to tell the registration number of the vehicle to him and the injured had told the registration number orally to him.

The Tribunal sought clarification from the Investigating Officer as to what was his explanation for the fact that, in the complaint dated 21.02.2022, the petitioner had stated that he had noted down the registration number of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: Nowhere in the deposition of the Investigating Officer came on record that he along with the wife of the petitioner had taken the photographs of the offending vehicle from CCTV camera.

The Investigating Officer neither did any investigation as to fix and ascertain that it was the offending vehicle with which the accident in question was caused and also that at the time when the respondent no.1 was driving the offending vehicle he was driving it rashly and negligently, which caused the accident.
It may be noted that rashly or negligently is an opinion which has to be formed on the basis of facts which have to be found out by the investigating officer by doing the investigation.

In the name of investigation, the maximum: what the Investigating Officer is doing, he takes the statement in which the reference to the vehicle being driven rashly and negligently is given or if not given then included by the Investigating Officer in Urdu or Persian language of which the personal statement is being taken would be oblivious and on such statement the Investigating Officer comes to his own conclusion regarding the vehicle being driven rashly and negligently oblivious of the fact that rash and negligence is not a fact and the Investigating Officer is duty-bound to investigate the facts and circumstances of the case.

Investigation is not a process of collecting opinions and on the basis of opinions the Investigating Officer forms his own opinion and files the charge-sheet and/or DAR.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is settled proposition of law that, in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine-qua-non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.
A holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an enquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
However, that does not mean that a Tribunal which has been approached with a claim for compensation under the Motor Vehicles Act should ignore all basic principles of law in determining the claim for compensation.
The relevant provisions of the Act are not intended to jettison all principles of law relating to a claim for compensation, which is still based on a tortious liability.
It has also to be kept in mind that after the accident whatever the injuries the petitioner might have received the petitioner was in a position to call his uncle Bhupinder Singh on his mobile phone intimating him regarding the accident.
The facts of the case which has come after the examination of the owner of the offending vehicle are such which raises reasonable doubt as to the veracity of the case of the petitioner and in such a situation the delay in the registration of FIR is the material fact.
Generally, whatever investigation is done by the Investigating Officer is done while he is accompanied by another police official and this is a check that the Investigating Officer does the investigation in the presence of another witness and it minimizes the chances of false investigation by the Investigating Officer.
26. In the present case, the Investigating Officer saw the registration number of the offending vehicle in the mobile phone, however, neither the Investigating Officer seized the mobile phone not took any photograph/ copy of the photograph in which the registration number of the offending vehicle was visible.
The manner in which the Investigating Officer did the investigation as far as ascertainment of the registration number of the offending vehicle is concerned is done in highly irresponsible manner and not only that, the SHO and/ or other supervisory officers also did not supervise the investigation by the Investigating Officer nor guide the Investigating Officer to do the investigation in a proper manner.
27. The claim preferred under section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act or DAR which is treated as claim petition under section 166 (3) of Motor Vehicles Act and before the claim petition can be allowed, it has to be proved on the balance of probability that the accident in question was caused because of any rash or negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Nowhere in the deposition of the Investigating Officer came on record that he along with the wife of the petitioner had taken the photographs of the offending vehicle from CCTV camera.
The Investigating Officer neither did any investigation as to fix and ascertain that it was the offending vehicle with which the accident in question was caused and also that at the time when the respondent no.1 was driving the offending vehicle he was driving it rashly and negligently, which caused the accident.
It may be noted that rashly or negligently is an opinion which has to be formed on the basis of facts which have to be found out by the investigating officer by doing the investigation.
In the name of investigation, the maximum: what the Investigating Officer is doing, he takes the statement in which the reference to the vehicle being driven rashly and negligently is given or if not given then included by the Investigating Officer in Urdu or Persian language of which the personal statement is being taken would be oblivious and on such statement the Investigating Officer comes to his own conclusion regarding the vehicle being driven rashly and negligently oblivious of the fact that rash and negligence is not a fact and the Investigating Officer is duty-bound to investigate the facts and circumstances of the case.
Investigation is not a process of collecting opinions and on the basis of opinions the Investigating Officer forms his own opinion and files the charge-sheet and/or DAR.
